title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: a save or delete that names no package addresses the one package's row, and a name two packages hold is refused 409 (#23165)
body:
Fixes #23165
Clause-②: yes (narrowing): a package-less save or delete of an item two or more packages hold is refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, as is a package-less save of an item a read-only package holds. One request class flips 409 → 200, as #22128 declared for the same flip: a package-less save that carries the package row's `If-Match` token (the token now names the row the save writes). The published `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId` describe changes, and `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema` gains an optional `packageId`.

## What this does

Option B under ADR-0070, the direction triage gave in `6141939797`, for both doors. It resumes `claude/issue-23165-direct-save-resolves-package@cd7d91390` (the save half, measured in `6141156635`), with `origin/main` merged in by a merge commit. Nothing from the resume branch is reverted.

One resolution, `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.packagelessAddress` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`), answers "which row does a write that names no package address". It reads the item's environment rows at the write's state, with the canonical type and the bundle member, and no package predicate:

| the item's rows are bound to | direct save naming no package | delete naming no package | the read's `version` (no package) |
|---|---|---|---|
| one package `P` | writes `P`'s row, as `?package=P` does | removes `P`'s row | `P`'s row's token |
| two or more packages | refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, names them, writes nothing | refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, names them, deletes nothing | the package-unbound row's (as before) |
| no package | the package-unbound row, as before | the package-unbound row, as before | as before |

Three readers call it: the direct save, the delete (its draft discard reads the draft rows), and `readVersionToken`. The draft save keeps `SysMetadataRepository.resolveWriteHead` and is not routed through it, because that would not be a pure refactor: with two packages the draft save binds to the first active row in storage order, and the new function refuses that case. `SysMetadataRepository`'s defaults are unchanged, since its four `null` callers mean the unbound row.

Governing text, as the release `6141220035` quotes it:

> **ADR-0070 (Accepted), TL;DR 1:** "The "package-less / `sys_metadata`-scope" state stops being an authoring destination; it remains only as a read-side rehydration detail and a migration source."
> **ADR-0048 §3.3:** "A *context-free* read (`getItem` with no package id) is best-effort: it returns the first match and the caller is expected to pass the package id when it cares."

## The delete door: measured, and where the file surface grew

**Measured first:** the delete door could not name a package at any layer. `deleteMetaItem` had no `packageId`, `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema` declared none, and `META_ITEM_RESET_PARAMS` did not hold `package`, so `DELETE …?package=` was refused 400 as an unknown parameter. Every delete was package-less, and `repo.get` / `repo.delete` each took the first row a package-agnostic `findOne` met.

Implementing the refusal triage ordered with no way to name the package would leave a two-package item with no delete at all. So the delete gets the address the save already has:

- `deleteMetaItem({ …, packageId })`. Named, it removes that package's row and no other. Absent or `null`, the resolution above applies.
- `DELETE /api/v1/meta/:type/:name?package=PACKAGE_ID` reads the parameter through `metaItemPackageBinding`, the same reading the PUT, GET and publish doors of the item use: `all` and the empty value name no package. `package` joins the door's closed set (`META_ITEM_RESET_PARAMS`) and its repeated-parameter guard.
- `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId`: an optional, nullable request key whose describe mirrors the save's.
- The in-process package-scoped callers name their package. `deletePackage` (uninstall) and `discardDraftInItsScope` (`discardPackageDrafts`, `revertStoredPackage`) deleted each of their items by name only. For a name two packages hold, that could remove the other package's row and leave their own. Without a named package they would now be refused; with it they remove exactly their own row.

These are outside the claim's listed surface (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema`), and the reason is the measurement above. They sit in separate commits (`ddf0177ef` for REST and spec), so they can be split off if the seat rules otherwise.

**The delete receipt, measured in every branch.** "It no longer exists" and "reset to artifact default" were true only when no other row of the item remained. That already failed at the base whenever two packages held the item. With a named delete, it would fail for every delete of one package's row. The receipt now names the package it removed from, and when another row is still stored it names that row instead of claiming the item gone. A delete of the package-unbound row with nothing left reads byte for byte as before. Probe readings on the final code:

- one package: `Deleted app 'a1' (package=com.qa.lanebapp) — it no longer exists. [seq=2]`
- two packages, a package-less delete: `Name the package this delete is for, then send it again: on the REST door add ?package= with the package id, in process pass packageId. Nothing was deleted. app 'a2' belongs to 2 packages ('com.qa.lanebapp', 'com.qa.otherapp'), and a delete that names none has no single row to remove.`
- two packages, `packageId: com.qa.lanebapp`: `Deleted app 'a2' (package=com.qa.lanebapp), and it still exists: its row bound to package 'com.qa.otherapp' remains. [seq=5]`
- a named package with no row: `No row of app/a2 is bound to package 'com.x', so nothing was deleted: its rows bound to packages 'com.qa.lanebapp', 'com.qa.otherapp' remain.`
- a package row with a package-less row beside it: `Deleted app 's6' (package=com.qa.lanebapp), and it still exists: its package-less row remains. [seq=4]`

## Known residue, not converted here (S6)

The card's existing-rows line holds: a package-less row stored beside a package's row stays as it is. Where that package-less row was stored first, the read naming no package keeps serving it (ADR-0048 §3.3's first match), while a package-less save writes the package's row and a package-less delete removes it.

This is **reachable through today's doors on this branch**, not only through rows minted before the fix. A package-less save of an unbound item writes the unbound row. A save of the same item naming a package then writes a second row beside it, and the unbound row comes first. Measured over the protocol doors at this branch:

- rows: `[null, "unbound"]`, `[com.qa.lanebapp, "pkg"]`;
- read with no package → `unbound`; read with the package → `pkg`;
- a package-less save → receipt `package=com.qa.lanebapp`, writes `third` into the package row;
- read with no package afterwards → still `unbound`; the list serves `third`.

It is reported as an out-of-scope finding for the seat to file. The producer is the save that names a package beside an existing package-less row of the item, which is outside this card's direction.

## Pins

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.packageless-save-address.test.ts`: the resume's 14 save pins, plus 12 for the delete door. The engine double keeps its rows and is pinned to the producer's dispatch predicates, and the ledger records it (`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`). The delete pins:

- the delete → read round trip (one package);
- the read's token is accepted by a pinned delete;
- the package-less draft discard removes the inherited draft;
- two packages, on the delete and on the draft discard: refused `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`/409 (`code` + `status` through `resolveThrownHttpError`), naming both, nothing deleted;
- naming one package removes only its row, the other row is served, and the receipt names what remains;
- naming a package with no row removes nothing;
- an uninstall, and a package draft discard, that remove only their own package's row;
- control: the unbound item, with its receipt byte for byte;
- control: the package-row-plus-package-less-row residue.

`packages/rest/src/meta-draft-head-package-inheritance.test.ts`, real `RestServer` routes over better-sqlite3:

- the card's probe through PUT, GET and DELETE;
- two packages refused 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` on PUT and DELETE, nothing changed, and `DELETE ?package=` removing that package's row only;
- the unbound control.

`packages/rest/src/rest-server-meta-member-selector.test.ts`: the reset door's measured set now includes `package`. A preservation pin shows `?package=` reaching `deleteMetaItem` as `packageId`, with `all` and the empty value naming none. A refusal pin shows a repeated `?package=` answered 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` without the protocol being called.

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts`: `packageId` is preserved through parse, `null` is accepted, and a non-string is refused.

**Fixture triage, one case replaced:** in `meta-draft-head-package-inheritance.test.ts`, the #22128 rider case "active, no row at the env-local address: the read serves `null`, and `If-None-Match: *` creates it" pinned the defect itself: a package-less save minting an env-local row beside the package's row. It went red on the merged tree. The replacement pins the rider's invariant at the address the save now resolves:

- the read's token is the package row's;
- `If-None-Match: *` is refused 409 `METADATA_CONFLICT` with that token as `currentVersion`;
- `If-Match` writes the package row.

The draft path's existing pins are unchanged and green.

## Reverse verification

Every leg ran with the fix committed first. Each swap wrote the merged-base blob (`8aff9accc`: the resume's save fix, no delete door) into the working tree only, under a trap. The swap was proven on disk (`git hash-object` equal to the base blob), and the restore was proven by the blob equalling HEAD, an empty `git diff HEAD` and a clean status. The subjects resolve through `src` (relative imports), so no `dist` was involved. Ordinary red in both directions.

- **`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`** → base blob `024ecc299`, over `protocol.packageless-save-address.test.ts`. Predicted 8 red / 18 green; measured `Tests  8 failed | 18 passed (26)`. The 8 are the predicted ones: the delete round trip, both two-package refusals, the named delete, the named delete with no row, the uninstall, the per-package draft discard, and the residue receipt. Restored: blob == HEAD `66d88b24a`.
- **`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`** → base blob `9a64fac24`, over `rest-server-meta-member-selector.test.ts` and `meta-draft-head-package-inheritance.test.ts`. Predicted 4 red; measured `Tests  4 failed | 40 passed (44)`: the reset door's measured set, the `?package=` preservation pin, the repeated-`?package=` refusal, and the real-route named delete. Restored: blob == HEAD `78f538b46`.
- **Type-level, the rest door's request literal against the rebuilt `@objectstack/spec` declarations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 → 0 each leg, restored blob == HEAD):
  - leg A: a direct `packageId: deletePackageId ?? null` compiles (`tsc --noEmit` exit 0);
  - leg B: `packageIdx:` fails `TS2561 … 'packageIdx' does not exist in type 'TransportScopedMetaRequest(…)' … Did you mean to write 'packageId'?` (the type it prints, spelled here without angle brackets, lists `packageId?: string | ... 1 more ... | undefined`).
  - So rest reads a declaration that carries the new key.
  - A first attempt at this leg was a **no-op**: its replacement contained its own anchor, so `ablation-replace` refused it (anchor 1 → 1) and restored without running `tsc`. That reading is void, and the two legs above replace it.

## Tests and gates

The head is `b546c5ff2`. The gate union ran after that final commit. The suites ran at `2ceb726ce`, the merge of `origin/main` @ `4f5679c26`. The one later commit, `b546c5ff2`, touches only the two corrected doubles, and those two files were re-run there. All runs used the verify lock and rebuilt `dist`.

**Suites**

- **metadata-protocol, whole suite** (`2ceb726ce`): `Test Files  235 passed | 3 skipped (238)` · `Tests  28328 passed | 19 skipped (28347)`.
  - Before the fixture correction it read `2 failed | 232 passed | 3 skipped`, `10 failed`.
  - The 10 were `protocol.delete-receipt-wording` and `protocol.delete-object-registry-unregister`. Their rows had no `package_id` key and their strict matcher missed `package_id: null`; their `find` answered `[]` for every table.
  - Corrected to rows as stored (`package_id: null`), with a `sys_metadata` `find` that holds the caller's `limit`. No assertion changed.
  - At `b546c5ff2`: `Test Files  2 passed (2)` · `Tests  22 passed (22)`.
- **The resume's pins on the first merged tree** (`8aff9accc`): `Test Files  8 passed (8)` · `Tests  24521 passed`, the same count the previous report gave.
- **rest**: 7 files, the reset door's selector and multiplicity pins, org-scope, #22128's real-route file, publish scope, version-token OCC and the new query-decision file → `Test Files  7 passed (7)` · `Tests  141 passed (141)`.
- **spec**: `src/api/protocol.test.ts` → `Tests  186 passed (186)`.
- **Typecheck**: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/spec`, all exit 0.
- **Generated artifacts**: `@objectstack/spec check:generated` exit 0 on the merged tree. `check:docs` was the only stale artifact after the describe edits, and it was regenerated in `389e545a4`, beside the authorable-surface row for `DeleteMetaItemRequest:packageId`.
- **Consumers** (they resolve `metadata-protocol` through `dist`, rebuilt first: `dist/index.js` holds `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal` ×4, `remainingRowsPhrase` ×3, the old name ×0). Measured at `e9b1744ef`, before the second merge. The merge brought other regions of `protocol.ts`, and the full suite above covers it.
  - objectql: 15 files that drive delete, uninstall, publish and lock → `197 passed`;
  - plugin-security: 4 permission-set files → `110 passed`;
  - runtime: 3 files (packaged-base lock, read-your-writes, uninstall org scope) → `34 passed`.
- **CLI**: no file under `packages/cli` is in the diff, so no unit layer is owed. `security-catalog-overlays.integration.test.ts` holds single-row groups only, and is declared to CI.

**Gates** (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, no paths, at `b546c5ff2`)

- 122 commands, each exit code recorded before any pipe. 122 of 122 exit 0.
- `--ran`: `Run reconciliation — 122 derived, 122 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.`
- The first union, at `2ceb726ce`, found:
  - `check:objectql-double-limit` red on the two corrected doubles' new `find`, fixed in `b546c5ff2`;
  - `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` at exit 3 (prerequisite: `dist` not built). A full `turbo run build` (74/74) cleared them before this union.
- Size: 1,188 changed lines (+1,157 / −31) in 14 files, under the 3,000 human-merge threshold.

**Lint**: a narrowing, with all three pieces of evidence.

- ① The population: the diff's 10 `.ts` files. Its 4 other files are `.md`/`.mdx`/`.json`, outside `eslint.config.mjs`'s `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` globs.
- ② `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on them reports 10 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 ignored.
- ③ `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (its own header: "no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules ... for ANY file"), so this diff cannot move a verdict on any untouched file.
- The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes (not filed)

- **The registry heal after a delete that leaves another row stored.** `restoreArtifactRegistryView` drops the runtime shadow whatever remains, at base and here alike. The store-backed reads serve the remaining row, as pinned. What the registry serves until the next hydration is NOT MEASURED. Carrier: none.
- **The control-plane legacy raw-engine delete** (code-only types `job` and `agent` on a kernel with no environment) still removes the first row of `(type, name)` with no package. It is unchanged, narrow, and outside the repository path this card resolves. Carrier: none.
- **The draft save with two packages** binds to the first active row in storage order (`resolveWriteHead`, #11087). This is unchanged, per triage. The save describe keeps its "the item's active row" wording rather than writing a driver-order pick into the contract.
- **plugin-security**: once this lands, `storedRowPackageArg` (#21861) is redundant. `permission-set-projection` and `position-write-through` delete by name with no package, so a name two packages hold is now refused loudly where it used to remove one row silently. Carrier: the plugin-security lane. ⛔ Nothing in `packages/plugins/**` was edited.
- **SDK / console**: `@objectstack/client`'s `meta.deleteItem` and objectui's `metadata-client.reset` send no package, so they cannot use `?package=` yet. Carrier: objectstack-ai/objectui#12300 (the console half) for the console; none named for the SDK.
- **The CLI's `os migrate security-catalog-overlays`** drains a group of same-name rows by repeated package-less deletes. A group of one package row plus a package-less row still drains, package row first. A group bound to two packages would now be refused rather than drained. Its integration test holds no such group. The integration tier is declared to CI.
